topic.title: Lac-Mégantic: a parked oil train with too few hand brakes rolled away once its locomotive's engine was shut down after a fire

description:
How did a train with no one aboard reach Lac-Mégantic at full speed?
It was parked on a hill for the night. We rebuild it in 3D: the hand brakes, the brake test, the fire, and the air that slowly leaked away.

topic.title: One Phone Call Doubled the Load on This Walkway

title: The Hyatt Walkway Collapse: One Phone Call Doubled the Load
description:
In Kansas City, two steel walkways hung above a crowded hotel atrium on thin rods. Why did they fall?
This is the full cause chain from the federal investigation: a connection that was already too weak, a change agreed by phone during construction, a connection that nobody calculated, and the nut that pulled through its beam.
Then what the investigators measured in their lab, and the rule every engineer works under because of it.

topic.title: The Gauge Said Normal. The Tower Was Nearly Full.

title: The Gauge Said Normal. The Tower Was Nearly Full.
description:
One March morning a distillation tower at the BP Texas City refinery was started up after maintenance. Its level gauge said the liquid was low. It was nearly at the top.
We rebuild the unit in 3D and follow the U.S. Chemical Safety Board's investigation: a tower filled for hours with nothing taken out, a gauge that could only see the bottom of it, an old vent stack with no flare, and trailers parked close by.
Then what the board found, and what it asked the industry to change.

title: The Titan Submersible Implosion: What Really Happened
description:
A carbon-fibre submersible dived toward the wreck of the Titanic with five people aboard and never came back up.
We rebuild Titan in 3D and follow the two investigations, the NTSB's and the U.S. Coast Guard Marine Board's: a hull nobody certified, a loud bang on an earlier dive, warnings that were set aside, and the last minutes of the dive.
Then what both boards found, and what they asked to change.

topic.title: Why Airline Pilots Now Need 1,500 Hours

title: The Colgan Air Crash: The Stall Warning That Rewrote Pilot Rules
description:
A turboprop airliner on a winter night approach to Buffalo got a stall warning, and the pilot pulled the wrong way.
We rebuild the Colgan Air crash of February 2009 in 3D and follow the NTSB's investigation link by link: a landing speed set too low for the ice, talk below ten thousand feet, a warning band nobody called, and the last half-minute of the flight.
Then what the NTSB found, and the law that now asks every US airline first officer for 1,500 flight hours.

topic.title: The Ohio State Fair Fire Ball Accident

title: Ohio State Fair Fire Ball Accident: The Rust Nobody Saw
description:

We rebuild the Fire Ball in 3D and follow the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's investigation: a hollow steel arm, water and rust working from the inside for years, and inspections that could only look at the outside.
Then what the safety alert, the CPSC and the state of Ohio asked to change.
